usageNotes: Use this to grow a QEMU VM disk; it returns a task UPID and executes asynchronously, so poll the task status before assuming completion. Only expansion is supported — shrinking is not allowed and will be rejected. The `size` field accepts an absolute value (e.g. `50G`) or a relative increment prefixed with `+` (e.g. `+10G`); after resizing the disk, the guest OS filesystem still needs to be extended from within the VM.

examples.summary: Add 20 GB to the primary virtio disk of VM 101 on node pve1

tips: Pass `digest` (from the current VM config) to guard against concurrent modifications overwriting each other.
After resizing, extend the partition and filesystem inside the guest — Proxmox only grows the virtual disk, not the in-guest filesystem.
Resizing an EFI disk (efidisk0) or TPM state disk (tpmstate0) is rarely needed and may cause boot issues; double-check before targeting those.
The VM does not need to be powered off for a resize, but live resize visibility inside the guest depends on the guest OS and disk bus type.
